records.content: Using only the supplied frozen synthetic sources A and B, summarize whether all-coordinate alignment necessarily improves fixed linear regression, compare findings/limits, and state one bounded unresolved question. Do not invent additional bibliographic metadata.

All-coordinate alignment does not necessarily improve regression. A v1 (2024-01-01), abstract paragraph 1, reports gains only for its tested nuisance shifts and degradation for response-related shifts; it supplies conditional empirical findings, not a universal theorem. B v1 (2024-02-01), abstract paragraph 1, provides an identifiability limitation for arbitrary target conditional-label changes. The findings are compatible: empirical gains on restricted shifts do not remove the general unlabeled identifiability barrier. A does not establish which unlabelled diagnostics reliably distinguish beneficial and harmful shifts, while B does not rule out useful guarantees under explicit restricted-shift assumptions. Within these two excerpts, a bounded question is which restricted shift assumptions and observable diagnostics can justify alignment without claiming identification for arbitrary conditionals. Neither excerpt establishes global novelty, and full methods/results are not supplied.
